CHIEF COMPLAINT
Shortness of breath.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Rachel is a 48-year-old female presenting with shortness of breath and palpitations that occur with mild exercise or walking, such as walking up her driveway. She reports these symptoms happen more often lately. She has recently increased her exercise to lose weight. Patient denies knowing if symptoms are related to her chronic back pain. She reports reduced smoking from 2 packs per day to approximately 1 cigarette per day. She has been taking Effexor for depression with variable mood control, noting some days she feels great and other days feels extremely low, possibly related to weather. Her chronic back pain is controlled somewhat with Neurontin but still occurs occasionally. She reports she does rest when pain is severe. She has not established a regular yoga habit as previously discussed.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Nurse completed review of systems. Patient denies any other issues bothering her today.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Depression, smoking history, chronic back pain.

MEDICATIONS
Effexor for depression. Gabapentin/Neurontin for chronic back pain.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Current smoker, approximately 1 cigarette per day, reduced from 2 packs per day. Exercising more recently. Has not established regular yoga practice.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Overall examination appears normal. Mild wheezes noted in all lung fields.

RESULTS
Pulmonary function tests suggest possible asthma or COPD. Chest X-ray shows flattened diaphragm consistent with COPD, commonly seen in smokers.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease) diagnosed. Patient counseled that COPD means inability to exhale appropriately. Started on Combivent inhaler 2 puffs twice daily to help open lungs. Prescribed albuterol inhaler 2 puffs as needed for acute shortness of breath. Prescribed prednisone taper pack. Continue Effexor as depression is stable. Continue Neurontin for chronic back pain. Encouraged to do yoga for depression and back pain management.
